overview: Adsorption is a surface phenomenon where a substance accumulates only at the surface of another; absorption is a bulk phenomenon where it is distributed uniformly throughout.
genZNote: Adsorption stays on the surface; absorption goes all the way in.

aspects.label: Where It Occurs
aspects.valueA: Only at the surface/interface of the adsorbent.
aspects.valueB: Throughout the entire bulk/volume of the absorbing material.

aspects.label: Rate With Time
aspects.valueA: Increases initially then reaches equilibrium as the surface saturates.
aspects.valueB: Remains uniform throughout, since it is a bulk process.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Gas molecules accumulating on activated charcoal's surface.
aspects.valueB: Water being absorbed uniformly throughout a sponge.

overlay.memoryTrick: Sorption (either process together) is called 'sorption' when it's unclear which of the two is occurring.
